title: Choose RepoMan's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Fact-Checker's Galley. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Fact-Checker's Galley
options.lineage: magazine fact-checking proofs — the checker's marked galley
options.thesis: Every claim runs as typeset copy; its check lives in the margin. The evidence is the layout, not a panel.
options.viewport: Two columns on one white sheet. Left, the findings as running typeset prose in rubric order, each requirement a heading. Right, a ruled margin: for every claim a small mono mark — ✓ verified, ◐ partial, — looked/not found, ✗ contradicted, ⚑ flagged — with locator and quote. Click a mark and the cited lines lift onto the proof beneath the claim, joined to the mark by a hairline. The decision (accept · override · your marks) is a pencil strip under each claim. Nothing is boxed.
options.risk: Serif copy can drift into 'editorial' if the margin stops doing the work — on the queue and the rubric screens too, not only the workspace. The margin discipline is the identity.

raised.raise: Enclosure never: no card boxes anywhere; hierarchy by rule, position and weight only.
Columns never move: the batch queue is a fixed ruled table and running rows update in place, cell by cell.
A drawn leader: opened evidence is joined to its margin mark by a hairline connector, like a wired schematic.
One vertical axis: a single margin rule that every finding on every screen hangs from.
Every state is a glyph and a word before it is a colour.
One ground: the paper floods the frame; no second panel colour, white is the only relief.

options.label: The Exhibit Binder
options.lineage: court exhibit binders — tabbed exhibits, index, stamps
options.thesis: Every finding is an exhibit: lettered, stamped, indexed, and cross-referenced like evidence entered at trial.
options.viewport: An index of exhibits down the left (A. Repository, B. Report p.9, C. Deploy capture…); the finding on the right reads like a filed memorandum citing exhibits by letter; a stamp block records state and the human's decision.
options.risk: The most familiar rendition of 'audit trail' — reads as a legal document, and it is where most runs in this category would land.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller Queue
options.thesis: A worked queue on an emissive black void: rank is depth, nothing is ever boxed, one bitmap face on strict baselines.
options.viewport: The batch queue as layered baselines; the submission needing a human most sits frontmost, brightest, widest.
options.case: Hackathon developers identify with it instantly; loses on clarity — reading cited code and a report page on a drifting black void fights the task.
options.risk: Reads as novelty on a projector, and a light rendition was inferred for the venue.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: The batch as a departures board: rows ranked live, columns fixed, values flip in place as runs progress.
options.viewport: Thirty submissions as ruled rows; stage and coverage flip character by character as the pipeline advances.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the queue — live rows are exactly the run status — but the judge does not identify with a station, and the workspace has no board to be.
options.risk: Carries one screen brilliantly and the other two not at all.

options.label: Man-Machine Wiring
options.thesis: Neon line diagrams on a strict traffic grid; red, amber, green as signal.
options.viewport: Findings wired to evidence as a lit schematic.
options.case: Traffic-signal colours read as a grade before the human decides — the one thing the product forbids.
options.kept: The drawn connector from label to node.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: Abyssal blue deepening by stage, one vertical depth axis ruling every line.
options.case: No judge identifies with a dive; depth-as-stage obscures four flat finding states.
options.kept: One vertical axis every line of copy hangs from.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre lighting cyc, night to day
options.thesis: State as light phase across horizon bands.
options.case: State-as-light is the least legible possible encoding of VERIFIED vs UNVERIFIED for a judge in a hurry.
options.kept: Named phases with labels so colour is never the sole signal.

options.label: Yé-yé Pop Sleeve
options.thesis: One flat saturated ground, a cropped portrait, four tracks in a corner.
options.case: A closed set of four items cannot hold thirty submissions and twelve requirements.
options.kept: One ground floods the frame; white is the only relief.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean review tool: sidebar, table, detail panel, one blue — executed at Linear's level of craft.
canonCard.viewport: Submissions table on the left, finding detail on the right, status pills in every row.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other reviewer tool by design; the 'best-designed thing at the event' bar is hard to clear from here.
